questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The unique culture of Berlin. Always wanted to stay there for a longer time than just vacation. Also Academic level was high of European (non Elite British) standards.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university provided good communication from their coordinators through mail and information meetings. However the Enrolment process is very bureaucratic and non digital why there was a lot of information needed to be communicated

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mails and meetings from the Erasmus Coordinators

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The bureaucratic nature of the enrolment can be very confusing but I ended up not missing anything

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Ended up leasing room in a shared apparent on AirBnB for long-term, which was pretty easy to find. I'm sure there were better (and cheaper) options if one look into WG-gesucht or sites like that, but you have to be patience and 'create your own luck' (many people are looking for cheap rooms in Berlin), so I preferred the easier option

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's mandatory to buy a 'Semester ticket' (cost around 150€-200€ I think) which give you unlimited acces to public transport (even with your bike). Since Humboldt (at least for non-natural science studies) is very central and close to S- and U-bahn, it is very easy to get to the campus from anywhere in the city and you don't have to think about tickets. Also you can't really live on campus since the campus is like KU spread around the city

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have some student-housing through their 'Studentenwerk' which I did not really looked much into since I wanted to live with my girlfriend and it didn't seem like they offered apartments for two persons. Also it did not seem to that you could be certain to get anything. Most of the places I saw or heard about from other students were big dorm buildings not in the prime location and a bit expensive. However most places in Berlin are expensive and its easy to get around with public transport, so I wound probably have looked more into it if I were alone.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just a lot of stuff and surprisingly much you have to do manually (by showing up an talk to someone in the administration), but you get through it then it's not worse than that.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Can't remember it all to be honest. A lot of online stuff before you get there. Then you have to show up at campus at a special time to get a registration document so you can create your student card in two different machines at campus. (you want to do this as early as possible because you have unlimited public transport with this card and it can be expensive to buy single tickets all the time. You register for the examns (non-seminars) later but also need a special document you only can pick up at campus to do so. Just follow the emails from the coordinators and you will be fine even though it can be a bit confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Dedicated coordinator who wrote good mails and held meetings and were very friendly if you had questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not as sharp on registration for the seminars as I wanted to be. Seminars are courses with half the amount of lectures but with a term-paper instead of an exam. You have to register for these some weeks before teaching is starting in contrast to the normal cources were you do not register to attend lectures but have to register for the exam in the middle of the semester. (I got 2 seminars translated to 1 KU economics seminar which was very nice). If you do 5 courses (30 ECTS) you want maybe 2 or 3 seminars so you don't have to do 5 exams in a very short periode of time. Also the Seminars are small classes (max 20 people) so I would say the quality of the lectures is higher and topics mores specialised. However because there are only room for max 20 of each seminar, many of the interesting seminars are really popular and your chances of getting a spot very low. I didn't know that and therefore only applied for 2 seminars, thinking I would get both. I was lucky to get 1 but there had been over 4 times the amount of possible attendees who had applied in both of them. I wound therefore recommend people to register for many seminars to maximise their chances of getting a spot. There is only binding registration a couple of weeks into the seminar so if you get to0 many you can just register for your preferred ones. I ended up getting a second seminar because its deadline were later but again I was really lucky with that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As written above register for many seminars since you probably won't get a spot on all of them. The deadlines for registration can be several weeks before teaching start so look into this as soon as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The quality of the lectures and seminars I attended were very high. However I think the amount of available courses were a bit low especially when you have to pick 5 and some of them have overlapping lectures. There were a lot of micro theory were I would have liked some more Macro and Advanced econometrics

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Comparable to master courses at KU. Some of them have a big workload (2-3 papers to read every weak for 6 ECTS points) were others were more chill (look at the assignments every week). But the professors were sharp and into their subjects

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much the same for the classic courses. However some courses have exercises which basically just were second lectures with a PhD student instead of the professor. The Seminars had weakly lectures with weakly readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* European Economic History II 
* Advanced International Trade (ended up not finishing)
* Public Economics (ended up not finishing)
* Seminar: political economy of radicalisation
* Seminar: History of statistics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
European Economic History II was really nice. Intersting subjects, good papers for reading, and a really good professor who have written on the subjects himself. 
Seminar: political economy of radicalisation was probably one of the best courses I have experienced. Really well structured with good papers on many different aspects of political economy and discussions in class so you really got to understand the papers

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The semester ticket, but it gave unlimited public transport so I would probably have bought it even if it was not mandatory

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: They have good canines were you can choose som very cheap options. Also the coffee at campus is good and cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports to a good price. I would really recommend people to sign up to those before the semester start

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: look above

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Seems cheesy to write but off course you have to experience the electronic music scene in Berlin. There are so many good clubs so I would definitely recommend you try a lot of different ones since they all have their specialities. In the summer it gets really warm, so spend your daytime in the Summerbads. There is a nice one next to the olympia stadium were you swim in the olympic pool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy its not that different from Danish and everyone speaks English. However the Germans off course speak German with each other and may not be as comfortable speaking in English. If you have the opportunity I would therefore definitely recommend learning German to a level were you can understand conversations.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hard to meet people on campus, easier in sports or language courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You still had to were the mask in classes and public transport. However it is only public transport now.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The club culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find some social life as early as possible. Because I was with my girlfriend I probably did not think I needed it that much, but the hardest time away was when I missed more social life with friends. In this regard registering for sport courses is a good opportunity. Even though it is a bit expensive I would probably have registered for a language course also. Just a great way to meet people who are in the same situation as you (was for my Girlfriend)
2. Register for many seminars (if you are a Econ student) since you won't get spots on all of them. If you don't get a spot you can try to 'play the exchange student card' and get a spot anyway.
3. Use cantines for lunch and libraries for reading. There are some really nice spots around the city and you can use other universities' cantines and libraries as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Berlin clubs

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting a good social life up and going.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
